speaker: will_kemp
text: You brought a parcel to supper. That was a mistake, and I am already grateful.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It was tied at Henley Street. It can be opened without a company.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Feel the knot. Somebody in your house has a gift for keeping a thing shut.

speaker: alice_brambleby
text: Put it on the board. Let him tire himself. The supper is hot. The cord is not.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Fingers first. An honest man begins with his fingers.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It has been nine days on the road. It will not give to a thumb.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Teeth, then. I have put worse tools to a quieter night.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: You will not put nine days of road into your mouth.

speaker: alice_brambleby
text: Bleed on my board and you will hear about it.

speaker: will_kemp
text: A fork, then. Let us be civilized about a cord.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Now there is a fork in it. That is not an opening. That is a picture.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Then a speech. This knot was tied by a child with a genius for locks, and the father will not say which child.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will not say which.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Three of them at home. The room can be trusted with one name.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The room cannot. A month ago I promised not to carry every household joke out of Henley Street. I can feel this one assembling in my mouth, and I am not spending it.

speaker: alice_brambleby
text: Then stop giving him the pauses. He spends a pause faster than he spends a penny.

speaker: will_kemp
text: The table is with me. You can hear them hoping for the name.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The table may hope. The name stays where it was tied.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Give me the child and I will sit down.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: You are reading a cord. Leave it a cord.

speaker: alice_brambleby
text: Enough.

speaker: alice_brambleby
text: There. One stroke. The knife was for supper, and the supper may have it back.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Cut off in the middle by a practical woman. I had another sentence ready.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: You had a fork. You may have it back when it is out of the cord.

speaker: alice_brambleby
text: Two pairs of knitted hose. A cake. A slip of paper. That is the whole of it, and it did not need a speech.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The hose are for the winter. The cake is my mother's. The slip can be read without a prologue.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Read it. If it is a riddle I expect to be kept in the answer.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Susanna's hand. Nothing on it but whom.

speaker: alice_brambleby
text: Whom. Then it is for someone, and this table is not required to finish the sentence.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The word is the end. The hose and the cake are the part I am glad of.
